question: Q-BBW-01 - is code-table `delete` suppressed by REFERENCE COUNT or by configuration?

answer.mechanism: NEITHER a client-side reference count nor per-tenant configuration. `delete` is suppressed by a single server-supplied per-row boolean on the grid record: **isReadOnlyRecord**.
answer.proof: Observed. The Actions column (dataIndex `EditDeleteLink`) renderer, read live off the grid column definition, is literally: `var q=c.data.isReadOnlyRecord; ... if(!q){l=Ext.String.format(f.config.editDelStr,s,s)} else {if(f.config.editStr){l=Ext.String.format(f.config.editStr,s,s)}}`. isReadOnlyRecord=true renders `edit` only; false renders `edit | delete`. There is no count, threshold or usage lookup anywhere in the render path.
answer.whatSetsIt: NOT observable from the client. The FirmCode record itself exposes only 4 fields (Name, Description, Inactive, Available-for-Portfolios) - no owner/system/provenance/refcount attribute is surfaced. isReadOnlyRecord is computed server-side.
answer.implicationForD07: The reference-count reading in bbw-vs-american-freight.md §3 is NOT supported by the AF evidence and the distribution below argues against it. Lucernex is not demonstrably doing a Where-Used reference check on code-table values, so Q-BBW-01 should not be used to reopen ASG Edge+ D-07 on that basis.

contradictsEstablishedFact.claim: `AI Abstracted` (TableType 2094) HAD a delete action at American Freight; at BBW it does NOT.
contradictsEstablishedFact.nowObserved: At AF today, `AI Abstracted` (LxBOID 1308) has isReadOnlyRecord=TRUE and offers **edit only** - no delete. AF now matches BBW exactly on all three values.
contradictsEstablishedFact.likelyCause: AF has been upgraded from build 26.08.0.46 to 26.09.0.113 - the SAME build BBW runs. The AF/BBW row-action difference has disappeared along with the build difference, which points at a platform-seeding change in 26.09 rather than at tenant usage or tenant configuration.

evidenceAgainstReferenceCounting: `AI Abstracted` is isReadOnlyRecord=TRUE in EVERY table it appears in (2094 Contract Status, 2107 Facility Status, 2157 Covenant Status, 2181 Security Deposit Status) - while `Active`, `Open`, `Closed`, `Possession`, `Deleted`, `Not Applicable` sitting beside it in those same tables are all DELETABLE. In a training tenant with 20.4 GB of documents and live facilities, `Open` and `Active` are far more likely to be referenced than `AI Abstracted`. Usage cannot explain that ordering.
TableType 2157 `Covenant Status Code`: `Active` is DELETABLE but `AI Abstracted` is protected - the exact inversion of what a reference count would produce.

TableType 2022 `Contact Type Code` splits cleanly along provenance, not usage: the 10 generic values (Broker, Construction Manager, Employer, Equipment Manager, Landlord, Lawyer, Primary Owner, Property Manager, Team Member, Vendor) are ALL protected, while the 4 that look tenant-added (Client, Notice, Sales Reporting, `Third Party - ASG`) are ALL deletable.
TableType 2037 `Job Function Code`: the 3 platform roles (PS Administrator, System Administrator, Vendor Administrator) protected; the 4 lease-admin roles deletable.
TableType 2070 `User Class Code`: only `Default Security` protected; all 9 others deletable.

TableType 3006 `Key Date Type Code` contains TWO rows both named `Option` - LxBOID 3095 is protected, LxBOID 3116 is deletable. Identical name, opposite flag: the flag tracks the ROW, not the value's meaning.
bestSupportedHypothesis: Inferred: isReadOnlyRecord marks PLATFORM-SEEDED (vendor-owned) rows, which a firm may rename but not delete, versus firm-added rows which it may delete. This fits every mixed table above and explains the duplicate-`Option` case. It is NOT proven - the server does not expose the attribute - and the decisive test is cross-tenant (see openTest).
openTest: If isReadOnlyRecord is provenance, then a platform-seeded value should carry the SAME LxBOID and the SAME flag in both tenants, while firm-added rows carry tenant-specific LxBOIDs. If instead the SAME LxBOID shows a DIFFERENT flag in AF vs BBW, reference-counting (or per-tenant config) is proven. Requires the identical 207-table scan at BBW.
method: For each of the 207 TableTypes: GET /en/admin/FirmCodeEdit.jsp?&popupList=true&includeType=Manage&TableType={tt}, extract the grid `storeUrl` + fdName, then GET that store with start=0&limit=5000. Read-only throughout; no Save/Delete was ever issued.
